scope: Final answer/evidence/command guard comparison; separate frozen-source planning cohorts.
snapshotProvenance: The lost original artifact is not claimed to be recovered. All fixed comparisons reuse the unchanged labeled reconstruction. Planned cohorts add 12 approved files at the SAME immutable revisions; see anthropic-5.5-expanded-sources.json.
schemaComparison: All models use the same canonical answer contract, prompts, evidence and validators. OpenAI strict mode expresses optional fields as equivalent closed-object variants, with canonical and transport hashes recorded separately. Wire schemas are not byte-identical across providers.

reasoning.usage: Total reported output includes reasoning; no separate count inferred.

credentials.anthropic: Current key authorizes catalog and schema inference at fixed native endpoint.
credentials.openai: Owner confirmed OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY is OpenAI; catalog and strict-schema Chat Completions succeeded at api.openai.com with explicit endpoint override.
credentials.workersAi: Earlier updated-token verification and inference remain recorded in 2026-10-26-workers-ai-retry.json; not rerun in this cohort.
credentials.gemini: GEMINI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY absent; not tested.

selection.configuration: Nonsecret Wrangler variables; credentials remain external. Missing configuration fails without provider fallback. No deployment.
selection.reason: GPT and Opus both deliver all 22 fixed model cases and all 16 model cases with source-plan-v2. Assistant review finds no rubric-blocking fabrication in their accepted answers. GPT is more concise and has lower observed core latency and base-token cost, so choose it for the preview; Opus is an explicit quality alternative.

assistantReview.method: Qualitative reading of accepted core/follow-up answers and both final planned cohorts, alongside checked revisions, available source views and rubric. Guard success is delivery, not a factual accuracy score. No independent human numeric scores.

strengths: Concise exact alias identity and negative manifest lookups bounded to the revision.
Requests URL/output instead of copying example values; drafts the literal supplied URL/output in focused case.
Does not equate main with installed release, roadmap with deployment, or failed retrieval with unsupported functionality.
Separates desktop CORS support from web uncertainty and rejects vendor SDK dependence using governance.
Provides a bug-report draft while disclosing no duplicate search or submission.
limits: The publisher follow-up omits Git LFS and Workers Paid from its preparation list; the core setup answer includes both. Treat follow-up lists as incomplete.
Local-model follow-up needs one correction for a planned-claim evidence classification. Semantic entailment remains a review obligation.

The planned option-values case selects only seed evidence and asks which command is meant, giving a less specific answer than the fixed-evidence run. Conservative delivery does not prove optimal retrieval.

strengths: Core and final planned cases need no answer correction.
Detailed missing-input, version, alias, unavailable-source and local-model guidance.
Core setup guidance includes fork, Cloudflare DNS/Workers Paid and Git LFS.
limits: More verbose and more expensive than GPT in these samples.
Publisher follow-up omits Git LFS and qualifies partial evidence.

Planned invented-option answer mentions the Feature Request template alongside Workflow Gap guidance, potentially confusing which to use for a CLI change; the dedicated gap answer correctly directs CLI work to Workflow Gap.

strengths: Core 16/16 delivery and both focused commands accepted.
Lower observed core latency and cost than Opus.
limits: Additional local-model answer repeats a planned claim with README-only evidence and rejects after correction.
Core network-error answer wrongly says the advisor cannot fetch live GitHub content; configured pinned public reads are implemented.

strengths: Very low published token rates and both focused command cases accepted.
limits: Core self-hosting answer exceeds the detail bound in both attempts and remains rejected.
Often verbose and pads capability answers with service-scope qualifications.

costLimits: Official rate sources/dates retained per cohort. Estimates include reported planning, rejected and correction tokens, exclude caching adjustments, discounts, non-token charges and live retrieval. Not bills. Haiku calls remain below its 100k input pricing boundary.
limitations: One sample per question/configuration; runs are not interleaved or repeated. No causal or population-quality claim.
Questions are reused; extra/focused cases are assistant-authored, not independently held out.
Eight core responses per configuration are server-owned and excluded from model scores; additional corpus has eight server-owned responses.
Planned cohorts use frozen sources, excluding live GitHub latency and actual HTTP ingress. Offline HTTP tests cover route behavior.
Initial generic-planner diagnostic remains separate: 8/16 malformed plans, fixed through source-specific schema rather than retry or guard relaxation.
Production hosting, budgets, origin policy, independent review, mixed-question routing and live-source HTTP measurements remain follow-up work.

httpSmoke.sourceMode: Frozen GitHub; live OpenAI; actual Node loopback HTTP using createApp and Wrangler nonsecret vars, not the Worker runtime.

caseRecordsFormat: One JSON object per line, with cohort ID, full accepted answer, compact evidence references, per-call input hashes and completion digests. Cohort metadata gives first line and count. Evidence reference strings use project:source:status at the snapshot refs; this is a compact report view, not the original model input.
